commits_iter10.description: Phase A L1 (research_topics_2.md): 3 pure refactors in service of no-regression progress. (1) gpd_drone.py — cache drone mass in __init__ so step() no longer recomputes GRAVITY/9.81 each tick (exposes self.mass_kg attribute called out in the research doc). (2) scripts/visual_demo.py — consolidate the 200-sample deque + _trajectory_tracking_errors list into a single TrackingErrorAccumulator helper so the two views can no longer diverge (was the source of the iter-8 HUD/reporting-average mismatch). (3) planning/trajectory_optimizer.py — introduce PlannerConfig dataclass and wire ENTRY_EXIT_OFFSET + the 4 max_compression floors + the 2 helix-inflate knobs through it. Defaults preserve iter-9 values bit-identically. Unlocks per-race override without a code fork (the research_topics_2.md Phase A ask).

Phase A L1 end-to-end: RaceConfig carries planner_overrides / racing_line_overrides dicts populated from new top-level 'planner' and 'racing_line' sections in race_01.json. visual_demo.py constructs PlannerConfig and RacingLineConfig from the overrides (unknown keys ignored for forward-compat) and hands them to TrajectoryOptimizer and RacingLineOptimizer. race_01.json now carries the current iter-9 values explicitly. Future races can override any subset from their own JSON — the code-fork requirement (flagged by the research doc) is eliminated.

Phase A L1 runtime knobs: move PLAN_MAX_SPEED=4.0, MAX_CMD_SPEED=4.0, lookahead=0.3, search_window_s=2.0, proximity_pass_distance=1.2 out of visual_demo.py literals and into PlannerConfig + SequencerConfig, loaded from race_01.json. Extends planner section with plan_max_speed_mps, cmd_max_speed_mps, lookahead_s, search_window_s; adds new top-level 'sequencer' section with proximity_pass_distance. RaceConfig now also carries sequencer_overrides. Defaults preserve iter-9 values exactly. Drops the last 4 in-code magic numbers for this pipeline — research_topics_2.md's Phase A inventory now fully config-driven.
state.json — record iter-10 wrap-up + benchmark item #5 rejection.

Opt-in Butterworth-smoothed accel-FF infrastructure. Extends TrajectoryPoint with ff_acceleration field (default (0,0,0)); TrajectoryOptimizer pre-computes zero-phase low-passed acceleration scaled by PlannerConfig.accel_ff_gain and clamped to accel_ff_clamp_ms2 when gain > 0. visual_demo.py passes ff_acceleration as target_acc. Default gain=0.0 ⇒ target_acc=(0,0,0) ⇒ identical to iter-9 baseline (verified 3×). Addresses iter-9 backlog item #5 (smoothed accel-FF) as opt-in infrastructure — provides the 'target_acc hook' delivery path the research doc C3 ILC work will need without shipping any behavior change today.

C3 ILC runtime loader infrastructure. New module planning/ilc_runtime.py exposes ILCTable.load_from_json + clamped linear interpolation. PlannerConfig.ilc_table_path (default '') gates the load; when set, TrajectoryOptimizer overwrites each TrajectoryPoint.ff_acceleration with table-interpolated values, superseding the Butterworth path. Default empty path ⇒ no-op ⇒ baseline preserved. Provides the runtime half of research_topics_2.md C3. The offline calibrator half lands in a future iteration; this commit lets hand-authored or off-pipeline tables be tested today.

iter10_things_tried_and_rejected.result: Reverted. Port from find_closest to find_closest_forward broke the synthetic-benchmark's reported avg_tracking_error (0.67 m → 8.74 m, max 5.69 → 41.56 m).
iter10_things_tried_and_rejected.note: The research doc asserts benchmark.py has the same find_closest aliasing bug as visual_demo had pre-iter-8. But the two call sites have different *semantics*: visual_demo feeds the drone a closest-forward-lookahead target (progress moves with actual drone), so aliasing was a real bug. benchmark.py's synthetic sim feeds the drone a TIME-based target (trajectory.sample(sim_time)). Under time-based tracking, find_closest returning a cross-revolution point is arguably correct reporting ("closest point in space") whereas find_closest_forward reports drone's error relative to expected-progress. When the drone lags behind the time-based reference, the new metric balloons correctly but invalidates legacy threshold comparisons. Both readings are defensible; a proper fix would require introducing a separate 'closest-forward-progress' metric name without overwriting the existing one. Deferred.

iter10_opt_in_infrastructure.source: iter-9 backlog item #5 + research_topics_2.md C3 preparation
iter10_opt_in_infrastructure.description: TrajectoryPoint gains an ff_acceleration field (default (0,0,0)); TrajectoryOptimizer.optimize populates it with a zero-phase 2nd-order Butterworth low-pass of the generated acceleration, scaled by PlannerConfig.accel_ff_gain, clamped per-axis to accel_ff_clamp_ms2, when gain > 0. visual_demo.py passes ref.ff_acceleration as target_acc to GPDDrone.step. With default gain=0.0 the field stays at zero and target_acc=(0,0,0) — identical to the iter-9 no-FF baseline. The opt-in is flippable from race_01.json by setting planner.accel_ff_gain. Verified: gain=0 → 3/3 runs 12/12 × 0.665 m; gain=0.3 → ff_acceleration populated (max |a_ff|=5.0 m/s² at clamp), smoother than raw per-axis std. Infrastructure only; behavior change pending a future iteration willing to accept the regression risk of turning it on.

Runtime half of the C3 ILC loop. New module planning/ilc_runtime.py with ILCTable that loads a time-indexed ff_acceleration JSON (schema v1: samples=[{t, ff_acc[x,y,z]}], strictly increasing times, clamped endpoints). PlannerConfig gains ilc_table_path (default empty string). TrajectoryOptimizer.optimize loads the table (if path set) and overwrites each TrajectoryPoint.ff_acceleration with the interpolated value — superseding the Butterworth path. Empty path → no-op → baseline preserved. Unit tests: empty path returns None; missing path raises FileNotFoundError; valid JSON loads and interpolates endpoint-clamped; non-increasing times raise ValueError. Verified: 3 deterministic baseline runs at default empty path reproduce 12/12 × 0.665 m. Offline calibrator (the other half of C3 — iterate sim, Q-filter update, emit JSON) deferred to a future iteration.

iter10_refactors_shipped.change: GPDDrone.mass_kg attribute (cached in __init__). step() uses self.mass_kg rather than recomputing GRAVITY/9.81. Eliminates the iter-9 'hack' comment.

TrackingErrorAccumulator helper. Single API (append/average/clear/recent); owns both the full-trajectory list (for the PRD <0.5 m avg) and a 200-sample rolling window (reserved for HUD smoothing). Callers at line 515 and 580 now go through one object. _dataclass_from_overrides helper safely builds PlannerConfig / RacingLineConfig from race-config dicts.

PlannerConfig dataclass (entry_exit_offset_m, max_compression_{sturn,protected,helix,easy}, helix_{entry,interior}_inflate). TrajectoryOptimizer takes an optional planner_config; defaults match the iter-9 hardcoded values exactly. Replaces 7 magic literals with config-driven values without changing any of them.

RaceConfig carries planner_overrides and racing_line_overrides dicts; DroneRaceEnv.load_config reads optional 'planner' / 'racing_line' sections from race JSON. Empty sections (or missing ones) fall back to the dataclass defaults — pre-iter-10 configs load identically.

Added 'planner' and 'racing_line' sections with the current iter-9 baked-in values (entry_exit_offset_m=0.4, max_compression_helix=0.72, max_lateral_offset=0.6, smoothness_weight=0.40, etc.), plus 'sequencer' with proximity_pass_distance=1.2. PlannerConfig now also owns plan_max_speed_mps, cmd_max_speed_mps, lookahead_s, search_window_s. The race config is fully self-describing; second and third races can override any subset.

lessons_learned_iter10: Research doc's Phase A ask is *structural*, not a tuning change. Moving ENTRY_EXIT_OFFSET onto PlannerConfig doesn't move the drone's trajectory one micron; it just lets a second race override it without editing trajectory_optimizer.py. That's the whole win — the doc called it 'no algorithm risk' and iter-10 confirms: 3 deterministic runs reproduced 12/12 × 63.417 s × 0.665 m exactly.

The 'deque + list' pair in visual_demo.py was dead on the deque side — nothing read it — but the research doc flagged it anyway because the *shape* of that pair is the bug pattern: two parallel containers owned by the same updater. The consolidation into TrackingErrorAccumulator makes the divergence literally impossible to reintroduce.

iter10_infrastructure_added.change: GPDDrone.mass_kg attribute exposed. Used internally by target_acc feedforward; available to future callers (PyBullet ILC, centripetal FF) without re-deriving from GRAVITY.
TrackingErrorAccumulator class owns both full-trajectory and rolling-window views. Single source of truth for tracking-error samples.

PlannerConfig dataclass + optional planner_config argument on TrajectoryOptimizer.__init__. 7 previously-hardcoded values (ENTRY_EXIT_OFFSET, 4 compression floors, 2 helix inflates) are now config-driven with iter-9 defaults preserved. Prerequisite for research_topics_2.md Phase B (first-principles derivation) and Phase C (Bayesian auto-tuning).

lessons_learned_iter9: Baseline 12/12 + 0.665m is a FRAGILE EQUILIBRIUM. The 0.665m tracking error includes 36+ seconds of stall/limbo frames (t=10-47.6s) where target_source=='trajectory' but drone is stuck near gate-6 area waiting for the sim_time>2×total_time fallback trigger. Clean-tracking phase (t=0-10s) measures 0.4-0.7m — already near the 0.5m target on a per-frame basis.

ANY tracking improvement (centripetal offset, acceleration FF, tighter P gain, slower helix) fails gate-10 because the primary-PRD resolution depends on the drone stalling first. Stall → fallback → slow direct navigation → gate-10 passes at miss=0.48m. If drone tracks helix at design speed, it arrives at gate-10 too fast for the 82° off-normal pivot.

Acceleration feedforward via target_thrust += m·a_ref CANNOT be turned up without destabilizing the DSLPIDControl tilt-clamped thrust vector. At min-snap polynomial segment boundaries, a_ref has near-discontinuous spikes → attitude command spikes → attitude controller saturates → altitude loss → crash. Needs either a smoothed a_ref (low-pass filter) or a segment-aware FF gain schedule.

Tighter position gain kp_xy (0.4→0.6) dramatically improves pre-helix tracking (gate-3 miss 0.72→0.51, gate-4 miss 0.68→0.47) but the improvement is uniform across the race — which is exactly what overshoots the fragile helix-entry equilibrium.

The 'tracking error' metric as defined (|drone_pos - closest.position| where closest is on the ORIGINAL trajectory) actively penalizes approaches that shift target_pos away from ref. Centripetal position offset via target_pos += K·a_perp would need a correspondingly shifted metric to measure tracking quality — otherwise the metric measures the offset magnitude, not the tracking quality.

The 0.665m→<0.5m gap is genuinely STRUCTURAL. It requires ONE of: (a) joint fix of gate-10 structural issue (TOGT or Mellinger tangent constraints on min-snap) AND removing the stall, OR (b) metric refinement to separate 'clean trajectory tracking' phases from 'stalled/limbo' phases, OR (c) a smoothed acceleration-FF + per-segment gain schedule (not tractable in a single iteration).

improvements_backlog_remaining.rationale: Pre-optimize each gate's in-gate traversal point (2 free vars per gate, inside opening) to minimize turn angle. Directly addresses the off-normal gate-10 that forces the baseline stall. Would let the drone track the helix at design speed AND enter gate-10 correctly. Prerequisite for any tracking improvement. Complexity M per the doc — NOT compatible with 'without regression' scope (changes trajectory shape).

Constrain polynomial velocity direction at waypoints to racing-line tangent, removing ENTRY_EXIT_OFFSET auxiliary waypoints. Doc rates S complexity. Still carries regression risk: removing entry/exit waypoints changes polynomial shape, which in iter 9 was shown to break helix-entry equilibrium. Could land as a PlannerConfig opt-in flag for a future iteration.

Run ILC inside PyBullet so offsets match actual CF2X cross-track bias. Use the target_acc hook (iter 9 infra) to apply cached offsets at runtime. Complexity M. Requires a 5-8 × 60 s offline calibration run. Could land as a JSON-path opt-in in PlannerConfig (default empty → no ILC).

Apply target_acc FF with a gain schedule that ramps to 0 at each waypoint ± 0.1s (where min-snap has polynomial-boundary accel spikes), full gain in the middle of segments. Requires waypoint-time injection into the control loop.

Apply a 2nd-order Butterworth low-pass to ref.acceleration (cutoff 2 Hz) to smooth min-snap boundary discontinuities before passing as target_acc. Simpler than segment-aware but less precise. Good candidate for PlannerConfig opt-in flag.

Attempted in iter 10. Reverted: benchmark uses time-based sampling so the semantic differs from visual_demo — porting changes reported metrics from 0.67 m → 8.74 m which defeats 'without regression'. Proper fix would introduce a second metric name rather than overwriting the existing one.

Codex flagged 2s search window may alias if drone jumps >2s forward. Not observed but adding a monotonicity-only fallback (no window limit) would eliminate the theoretical edge case. Already config-driven post-iter-10 (PlannerConfig.search_window_s).

Derive PLAN_MAX_SPEED, max_compression_helix, proximity_pass_distance, search_window_s from drone physics + course geometry. Doc rates M / ~3 days. Incompatible with 'without regression' scope because the formulas do not exactly match the current hand-tuned values (e.g. 0.5 × min_opening = 0.3 m whereas current proximity_pass_distance = 1.2 m).

Bayesian optimizer over non-derivable knobs (smoothness_weight, corner_cut_aggressiveness, ILC filter cutoffs). Doc rates L / 1-2 weeks, overnight job. Requires faster sim loop. Standalone research deliverable.

iter9_infrastructure_added.change: GPDDrone.step() now accepts optional target_acc parameter (default (0,0,0), backward compatible). When non-zero, adds m·target_acc to the target thrust vector — the standard Mellinger/Tal-Karaman acceleration feedforward. Unused at iter 9 but available for future iterations pursuing the backlog items (PyBullet-native ILC, segment-aware FF, smoothed accel-FF).
